data.title: Tether Reports $191.5 Billion in Q3 Reserves and $1.5 Billion in Operating Profit
data.description:
Tether International, S.A. de C.V. released an assurance report prepared by BDO covering the third quarter of 2026, with data as of September 30. According to Odaily, Tether’s reserves totaled $191.5 billion at quarter-end, including $132.4 billion in direct and indirect U.S. Treasury holdings.

USD₮ issuance remained around $184 billion through the first three quarters, while cumulative net operating profit reached $4.5 billion. Third-quarter net operating profit was $1.5 billion, unchanged from the second quarter; U.S. Treasury securities and reverse repurchase agreements generated most of the revenue.

As of September 30, Tether reported total assets of $191.451 billion and total liabilities of $183.496 billion, leaving assets $7.955 billion above liabilities. Excess reserves increased to about $7.95 billion from $4.1 billion at the end of the second quarter.

data.title: St. Louis Fed President Alberto G. Musalem: Earlier Rate Hikes Could Reduce Economic Shock Risk
data.description: St. Louis Fed President Alberto G. Musalem said monetary policy and overall financial conditions remain accommodative, while inflation is still too high. According to Odaily, Musalem said inflation is unlikely to ease without Fed action and that raising rates earlier could reduce the risk of a shock to the broader economy.

data.title: AFT Sues Trump Administration Over Student Loan Forgiveness Delays
data.description: According to CNBC, the American Federation of Teachers sued the Trump administration Friday, alleging officials unlawfully blocked student loan forgiveness for tens of thousands of eligible borrowers. The lawsuit alleges Education Secretary Linda McMahon mismanaged the Public Service Loan Forgiveness program by miscounting payment timelines and failing to credit qualifying service. It also challenges delays in the PSLF Buyback program; 88,000 borrowers were still awaiting decisions as of the spring, according to a court filing. The Education Department said it was correcting coding errors from the Biden administration that had led to inaccurate payment counts.

data.title: Grand Canyon Inn Operator Files for Chapter 11 Bankruptcy Protection
data.description: Grand Canyon Hotel Services LLC, operator of the 101-room Grand Canyon Inn in Valle, Arizona, filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy protection on October 29 to restructure its debt. According to Sina Finance, court records show the company listed assets and liabilities in the range of $1 million to $10 million; it also operates seven other hotels across the United States. A 2025 wildfire that destroyed Grand Canyon Lodge and an August 29, 2026, flash flood damaged park infrastructure, while hotel occupancy and revenue in the area fell. The Grand Canyon Inn was listed for sale on July 14, 2026, for $7.95 million. A planned renovation of the company’s 28-room Grand Canyon Motel and construction of a 50-space RV park have an uncertain future as the bankruptcy proceeds.

data.title: Elon Musk's $119 Billion Terafab Faces Payoff Question Without Outside Customers
data.description: Elon Musk said Terafab is going well, but the planned Tesla and SpaceX chip plant in Texas, estimated to cost up to $119 billion, has no outside customers to share the bill. Korean supplier remarks cited by The Elec describe U.S. replies within 30 minutes to an hour, according to BeInCrypto. Tesla and SpaceX procurement staff visited about 10 Korean booths at SEMICON West, and more than half of those firms are discussing potential supply items. Terafab aims to produce 1 million wafers monthly within a decade; Intel joined as a technology partner in the spring. No fab has produced that volume solely for its owners, and Musk has never run a chip plant.

data.title: Binance News Update | Richard Teng: Binance Will Cover All Hacked Losses With Company Funds, $6.34 Billion Reserved and $5 Billion Already Held in the Affected Tokens
data.description: Binance CEO Richard Teng said the exchange will cover all losses from its security incident with company funds, having reserved more than $6.34 billion, $5 billion of which is already held in the exact tokens affected, including USDC, USDT, BTC, ETH and BNB. In a video message to users posted on X on Friday, October 30, Teng said customer funds were not affected, and shared new details about how the attack was carried out.“I want to be clear: we are committed to covering all hacked losses through our company funds,” Teng said. “Your assets are safe.”Built for the Long TermTeng said Binance can absorb a loss of this size immediately because of how it manages its own earnings. “Binance has always been built for the long term,” he said. “Most of what we earn from day-to-day operations is held in crypto assets. We have kept a lot of them in the company, and reinvested them — into the business, and into security. Because we believe in crypto, and in the long-term value of this industry.”That is why most of the affected tokens are already covered, Teng said. Binance is buying the remaining amount through market and OTC channels, and “the good news is that we are recovering stolen assets for users.”Customer Funds Were Not AffectedTeng addressed the question many users have been asking: how Binance can show their assets were not affected. “We never use any customer funds, so they are not impacted,” he said. “What was affected in this incident was Binance’s own hot wallet.”Under Binance’s security setup, most user assets are held in cold wallets and moved to a hot wallet only when a user makes a withdrawal. Teng encouraged concerned users to check their account balances and contact customer service with any questions.How the Attack Was Carried OutTeng said the attack was complex and not carried out by one person. Binance’s first findings pointed to a compromised laptop, and further investigation has uncovered additional points of breach.The attackers used EIP-7702, an Ethereum standard that lets a wallet delegate its execution to smart-contract code, to obtain on-chain execution approval over a Binance hot wallet. “That delegation did not pass through our normal approval controls,” Teng said. “That’s why we need to pause the withdrawal service to investigate, rebuild and retest the entire infrastructure system.”The attackers also used a self-destruct mechanism that “destroyed tooling and traces as they went,” he said, making the investigation harder. Binance is working with law enforcement, blockchain intelligence firms, token issuers and other exchanges to trace and recover the stolen funds, and about $3 billion has already been frozen with partners’ help. “We will do everything within our power to ensure that these bad actors will be held accountable,” Teng said.Withdrawals Expected Before SundayBinance is rebuilding its withdrawal service and will not switch it back on until it passes rigorous testing. “We are very hopeful that users will be able to withdraw prior to our Sunday deadline, which is on track to be within 40 hours,” Teng said.At the same time, Binance is running a full security review across the company, covering “endpoints, cloud, key management, signing. Everything.”Proof of Reserves by MondayOnce the remaining token purchases are complete, Binance will verify user assets through its Proof of Reserves. A full report is due by Monday, with an initial view possibly before then.Teng thanked industry partners, law enforcement and, “most of all,” users for their patience. “We will weather this storm,” he said. “Thank you for the support, and stay safe.”

data.title: Polymarket and Other Prediction Markets May Face Strict Australian Regulation; ASIC Has Received No Applications
data.description:
Australian Securities and Investments Commission Chair Sarah Court said at a parliamentary hearing that the regulator had received no applications from prediction market operators. According to Odaily, platforms such as Polymarket may face strict regulation in Australia, and applications for operating licenses would be closely reviewed.

Court said prediction markets use trading mechanisms similar to binary options, which are prohibited in Australia: outcomes are all-or-nothing, and the underlying events often have no connection to investments or financial markets. Australian users can access overseas platforms directly, but are not protected by local financial regulation and may lack access to dispute resolution and safeguards for customer funds.

data.title: Don Wilson Questions Hyperliquid's Information Priority, Position Transparency and Four Other Issues
data.description:
DRW founder and CEO Don Wilson raised six core questions about Hyperliquid, including information priority and position transparency. According to ChainCatcher, his comments came as the parent of the New York Stock Exchange considers bringing the decentralized perpetual futures platform to the U.S. market.

Wilson asked what advantages on-chain perpetual futures trading on a regulated exchange would offer. He said on-chain trading can reduce friction in trustless markets without identity checks, or allow buyers to receive purchased assets instantly through atomic transactions. But he noted that perpetual futures are not assets, so the latter benefit would not apply. Wilson also named Stan Druckenmiller and asked whether he understood that positions and trades on Hyperliquid can be tracked in real time, and whether he considered that an advantage.

Wilson questioned whether Hyperliquid’s priority-fee mechanism—which lets participants pay to see information earlier or move their orders ahead in the queue—aligns with the CFTC’s core principles. He also asked whether offshore and U.S.-based order-book liquidity could be combined and, if not, whether listing perpetual futures on a regulated exchange with a traditional centralized order book would be preferable to the inefficiencies of on-chain matching.

Intercontinental Exchange and trade[XYZ] previously announced plans to use Hyperliquid infrastructure to establish perpetual futures markets for crypto assets, stocks, commodities, foreign exchange and other real-world assets for U.S. traders, subject to regulatory approval. ICE would operate the regulated market and clearing structure. Wilson said the CFTC Chair Selig and the U.S. President Donald Trump administration should be credited with making such experiments possible, adding that markets would determine whether the arrangement was useful.

data.title: Binance News Update | Yi He: Binance’s Own Crypto Holdings Match Most of the $6.3 Billion in Affected Tokens; Withdrawals Expected Within 42 Hours
data.description: Binance CEO Yi He said on Friday, October 30, that the exchange’s own crypto holdings already match most of the tokens affected by its security incident, so only a small portion needs to be bought through on-exchange and off-exchange channels. The incident involved about $6.3 billion in assets, she said, and about $3 billion has been frozen with help from industry partners. Binance will use its own funds to match the affected assets in full.Most Affected Tokens Already CoveredYi He explained that Binance’s daily revenue and assets are held mostly in crypto, matching the majority of the tokens taken. That means Binance does not need to put the full $6 billion-plus into the market to buy new tokens. The exchange said earlier that $5 billion of its $6.34 billion reserve is already held in the exact tokens affected. Yi He thanked industry partners for their help in freezing assets.Withdrawals to Resume Within 42 HoursWithdrawals, paused for nearly a day to protect remaining assets, are expected to resume within the next 42 hours, Yi He said. The team is rebuilding the security environment and wallet settings and conducting security reviews. Withdrawals will reopen only once the environment is confirmed secure and user assets are protected.Proof of Reserves Update ComingBinance will update its Proof of Reserves in the coming days so users can verify their assets, Yi He said.Investigation and Next StepsThe security and technology team’s review so far shows the incident was a complex, multi-faceted attack, Yi He said, and Binance will proceed with extra caution. The exchange plans to publish a detailed technical security audit report and invite industry participants to help build shared security standards. Yi He said Binance will not stop pursuing the attackers, and will work with law enforcement worldwide to investigate the attack team and trace the stolen funds, while increasing its investment in security.

data.title: Lower-Priced Cars Sold Up to 20% Faster From First to Third Quarter
data.description: According to CNBC, Edmunds data showed that the time needed to sell vehicles priced from $20,000 to $29,999 fell 20% from the first quarter to the third, the largest acceleration among price segments. Vehicles priced from $30,000 to $39,999 sold about 18% faster, while sell times for those priced from $40,000 to $49,999 fell nearly 12%. The lower-priced tiers took fewer than 60 days to sell, while every segment above $50,000 took more than 60 days.

data.title: STOCKS | Polaris CFO Plans to Resume Stock Buybacks in 2027 After Two Years of Difficulty
data.description:
Polaris CFO Bob Mack said the company plans to resume stock buybacks in 2027, prioritizing the use of repurchases to offset share dilution. According to Sina Finance, the Minnesota-based off-road vehicle and boat maker suspended buybacks in 2024 as post-pandemic retail sales fell and it worked to reduce dealer inventories. Polaris (PII) had used buybacks to offset dilution from employee stock-based compensation and reduce its shares outstanding.

The company reported third-quarter net income of $38.4 million, compared with a net loss of $15.8 million a year earlier. Revenue rose 11% to more than $2 billion. Tariffs and inflation, including higher freight, fuel, aluminum and steel costs, remain significant headwinds. Polaris expects tariff expenses to reach $215 million this year, while commodity and logistics costs are expected to be $70 million higher than in 2025.

Polaris has generated cash through internal cost reductions and received about $80 million in tariff refunds to repay debt. As of September 30, its net leverage ratio—net debt divided by earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation and amortization—had fallen to 2 times from 3.4 times at the start of the year. Strategic business investments and dividends are also priorities.

Mack said the company’s ability to fund buybacks next year depends on the success of several new product launches and further improvements in operating efficiency. The possibility of continued commodity inflation also adds uncertainty to next year’s plans. He said buybacks remain a goal and described them as his ideal outcome. The company has not yet prepared its 2027 budget or cash flow forecast.

data.title: Digital Assets Week to Launch in Dubai With VARA as Host Partner
data.description: Digital Assets Week will launch its Dubai edition on 4 February 2027 at the Dubai Exhibition Centre, with the Virtual Assets Regulatory Authority (VARA) confirmed as Host Partner. The one-day conference will gather financial institutions, investors, regulators and infrastructure providers to discuss tokenisation, stablecoins, custody, DeFi and institutional digital-asset adoption, according to BeInCrypto. Following editions in London, New York and Hong Kong, the series will announce its first speakers and participating organizations in the coming months.

data.title: TRON Super Representatives Launch Vote on Proposal 108 to Optimize Contract Storage
data.description: TRON network Super Representatives have launched a vote on Committee Proposal No. 108. According to ChainCatcher, the proposal would enable the smart contract storage optimization feature introduced in GreatVoyage-v4.8.2.4 (Empedocles), with the changes expected to take effect on November 2 if approved. The optimization is intended to improve the stability and reliability of contract storage operations. Nodes experiencing block synchronization issues should be checked for the v4.8.2.4 upgrade.
